name: Elioenai
overview: Elioenai was a male descendant of the tribe of Levi, noted specifically as the son of Pashhur. He is uniquely identified in Scripture as the son of Pashhur who had married a foreign wife, a detail recorded in Ezra 10:22. There are no additional notes or significant events recorded about him beyond this lineage and tribal affiliation.
namesAndTitles: The name Elioenai means 'my eyes [look] to YHWH,' reflecting a devotional focus on the Lord. This proper name, as given in Ezra 10:22, indicates a personal or familial orientation towards God, though it was not explicitly given by God Himself.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Elioenai as a descendant of Pashhur, establishing a direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, there are no further family relationships documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Elioenai's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily genealogical, serving as a marker of the Levitical lineage during the post-exilic period. The mention of his father Pashhur's marriage to a foreign wife highlights the challenges faced by the returned exiles in maintaining covenantal purity. Elioenai's presence in Ezra 10:22 underscores the community's efforts to restore proper worship and obedience to God's law after the exile.
